note:
**The 1891 round - Cavendish Crescent South, Lenton Road and the whole of Park Valley.** RG12/2682, transcribed by A. Hagues. **Read to close the 1891 holes**, which [[every-census-gap-and-where-to-start]] now puts ahead of everything else in the record.

**Fourteen holes closed outright**, each a house the record held in 1881 and again in 1901 or 1911 but not in between:

| house | who |
|---|---|
| **15, 17, 19, 21 Cavendish Crescent South** | Maria Bell; Kate Green; Alfred Page the haberdasher; and **Mary Ann Allen, 80, with her daughter Sarah, 53** - Richard the bookseller having died |
| **1 Park Valley** (Arundel House) | **Arundel Preston, widow, 53**, with Charles, Arundel and Bracher, every age +10. Martin J Preston the solicitor has died |
| **3 Park Valley** | Robert Dennett the builder, 48 in 1881 and 58 here, now a widower |
| **5 Park Valley** | Frederick Pearson, ironmonger - the record has him here again in 1901 |
| **7 Park Valley** | Alfred Wilson, 61 in 1881 and 71 here, with Alice now married |
| **7 Lenton Road** | Rachael P Hutchinson, a daughter of 42 in 1881 and head of the house at 52 |
| **25, 29, 31 Lenton Road** | the Hopkinses; Frederick Carver; Henry Clarke |
| **Cliff House** | George Parr - **seventeen in the house**, eight children, two nieces, five servants |
| **Rock House, 37 Lenton Road** | Charles Shaw, 65 in 1881 and 75 here |

## Three things these pages settle beyond the gaps

**Cawson is Dawson.** [[1871-1881-duplicates-from-a-letter-or-two]] flagged Alfred Cawson at 11 Park Valley as probably my misreading rather than the index's. **It was.** The 1891 page gives **Alfred Dawson, lace manufacturer**, at 11 Park Valley plainly. Sarah beside him settles the second of the pair.

**13 Park Valley exists.** [[park-valley-13-missing-from-the-property-list]] noted that the 1881 round walks a number 13 the property list does not hold. Here it is again, ten years later, with **the same household** - Walter Wadsworth the lace merchant, his wife Elizabeth and their daughter Hope. Two rounds is not a misreading. The property wants creating.

**Ernest Jardine has his own house at 31.** At **19 Park Valley**, a lace machinist with a wife, a son of six and a daughter of three months. He was twenty-one and an assistant machine maker in his father's house at 25 Newcastle Drive in 1881 - see [[newcastle-drive-rule-name-before-number]], which that household settled. See [[ernest-jardine-at-19-park-valley]].

**The numbers at the top of the Lenton Road page are hard to read** - 25, 27 and 29 could each be taken for 75, 77 and 79. The households settle it: the Hopkinses are at 25 in 1881 and 1901, and Samuel Waite Johnson is at Lenton House, 27, in every other round.

**Three households are deliberately left out**, the record already holding them for 1891: Samuel Waite Johnson at Lenton House, James Bennett Gayton at 1 Holles Crescent, and William Barrett at 1 Park Drive.

**One cannot be filed.** Schedule 180 gives **5 Park Drive** and the record has no number 5 - Park Drive runs 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 9. The household is Margaret King Allen, widow, whom 1881 puts at **3** Park Drive with the same daughter ten years younger. Left rather than moved on a guess.
source: 1891 census enumerator's book RG12/2682, Lenton Road and Holles Crescent, transcribed by A. Hagues.
